subject: Difficulty: Cross-lagged Panel analysis -- fit.measures output

messages.author: efe1417fc0e545fe
messages.subject: Difficulty: Cross-lagged Panel analysis -- fit.measures output
parts:
Hi all,

I am Sam. I am using lavaan to conduct cross-lagged panel analysis, but i meet a difficulty about the model fit indices.I measured two variables at two times, and the syntax i used is shown below.


model <- 'T2D ~ T1D + T1V
              T2V ~ T1D + T1V'

fit <- sem(model, data = dataset)

summary(fit, standardized = T, fit.measures = T)

The difficulty i met is that the output does not provide Chi-square test, the other fit indices seems too prefect, and I can not figure it out why RMESA would be NA. 

  Comparative Fit Index (CFI)                    1.000
  Tucker-Lewis Index (TLI)                       1.000

Loglikelihood and Information Criteria:

  Loglikelihood user model (H0)              -2636.410
  Loglikelihood unrestricted model (H1)      -2636.410

Root Mean Square Error of Approximation:

  RMSEA                                          0.000
  90 Percent Confidence Interval          0.000  0.000
  P-value RMSEA <= 0.05                             NA

Standardized Root Mean Square Residual:

  SRMR                                           0.000

Thanks so much for your help, I spent a lot of time on it, but still no idea. Thanks.

Best regards,
Sam

messages.subject: Re: Difficulty: Cross-lagged Panel analysis -- fit.measures output
parts:
This is working as intended. 

Your model is saturated. It has no degrees of freedom. You are not testing anything. You will get the same regression coefficients result if you run two regression models: 

lm(T2D ~ T1D + T1V)

And:

lm(T2D ~ T1D + T1V)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Difficulty: Cross-lagged Panel analysis -- fit.measures output
parts:
Thanks. But, do i make it wrong? Coz I want to conduct a cross-lagged analysis. 

Did i use the incorrect syntax? Or cross-lagged analysis does not have fit.measure? Thanks a lot.

There's nothing wrong with your syntax.  You measured 4 variables, so there are 10 unique pieces of information in your data (4 variances and 6 covariances).  You are using those 10 "knowns" to estimate 10 unknown parameters (4 regression paths, 4 variances, a covariance between exogenous T1 variables, and a residual covariance between endogenous T2 variables).  Since you used all your information to estimate the parameters, there are no df left to test the fit of the model.  But the parameter estimates can still be interpreted.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
